Applicant :- Jai Prakash
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Yadav,Mukesh Singh,Prateek Tiwari,Sanjeev Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sanjay Tiwari Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Sanjeev Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sanjay Tiwari, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Rajeev Dhar Dwivedi, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
408 of 2023, under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC, Police Station- Chauri Chaura,
District- Gorakhpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and others and according to FIR, on the instigation of Suraj Kumar, informant became ready to purchase a land and in this regard, the alleged owner of the property, Jai Prakash executed an agreement to sell in his favour and Rs. 15 lakhs were also given to him by the informant but subsequently it was revealed that co-accused Nathuni was the imposter and he introduced himself as the real owner Jai Prakash.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that two cheques of total Rs.14 lakhs were given to applicant and subsequently after taking back cheque of Rs.9 lakhs, in his account Rs.9 lakhs were transferred and subsequently Rs.8.5 lakhs were transferred in the account of co-accused Bhagwant Kumar Bharti.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter and it appears that co-accused Bhagwant Kumar Bharti was the brother-in-law of the applicant, who used the account of the applicant and he firstly got transferred Rs.9 lakhs in the account of the applicant and thereafter he got transferred Rs.8.5 lakhs in his account.

He next submits, except the amount of Rs.9 lakhs, no other money was transferred in the account of applicant and therefore, it cannot be said that applicant committed any fraud and cheating.
5.
He further submits that even all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class.
6. He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 01.04.2024 i.e. for last more than eight months.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submit that co-accused persons are close relative of the applicant and co-accused Suraj Kumar is his son while co-accused Bhagwant is his brother-in-law and with the connivance of the applicant the fraud was committed and by playing fraud applicant and others duped Rs.15 lakhs of the informant, therefore, it cannot be said that applicant has not committed any offence but both the counsel could not dispute the fact that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 01.04.2024 i.e. for last more than eight months.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
9.

However, there is allegation that applicant alongwith others duped the informant and misappropriated his Rs.15 lakhs and a very handsome amount was also transferred in the account of the applicant but it also reflects, subsequently Rs.8.5 lakhs has been transferred in the account of co-accused Bhagwant Kumar Bharti from the account of the applicant.

10. Further, all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 01.04.2024 i.e. for last more than eight months.
11. Further, law is settled unless proven guilty, an accused deemed to be innocent.
12. Further, bail application should not be dismissed for punitive purpose and bail is a rule while bail rejection is an exception.
13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Jai Prakash be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
